newsitem.title: GREECE: DUBLIN EU SUMMIT TO FOCUS ON EMU, CRIME - IRISH PM.
newsitem.headline: DUBLIN EU SUMMIT TO FOCUS ON EMU, CRIME - IRISH PM.

text.p: Irish Prime Minister John Bruton, whose country holds the European Union presidency, said on Thursday the Dublin summit will focus on the single European currency and policies against organised crime and drugs.
"I would like to emphasise recent progress in finalising the arrangements for a single currency," he told reporters after meeting Greek Prime Minister Costas Simitis.
Bruton, who is touring EU capitals ahead of the December summit, also said the bloc will also aim to forge common policies to fight organised crime and narcotics smuggling.
He said no new treaty like the one signed in Maastricht would be achieved in Dublin but added there would be progress on the issue and a new pact could be reached at the next summit in Amsterdam.
Simitis said Greece will push at the summit for the EU retaining its present character of helping weaker members and forming common borders.
"We will stress the need for a common foreign and security policy," Simitis said.
Athens was the first stop on Bruton's agenda.
